tools.name: inspect_domain_dns
tools.description: Free. Audit one sending domain: MX hosts, SPF with every include expanded and the true DNS lookup count against the limit of 10, DMARC policy including inheritance from the parent domain, and published DKIM keys. Returns a grade and the fixes to make.

tools.name: audit_sending_domains
tools.description: Free for up to 3 domains per call. Audit several sending domains at once and get a grade, SPF lookup count, DMARC policy, DKIM status, MTA-STS (policy checked against the MX hosts), TLS-RPT, BIMI and fixes for each, plus a snapshot to pass to monitor_sending_domains later.

tools.name: monitor_sending_domains
tools.description: Free for up to 3 domains per call. Report what changed in SPF, DKIM, DMARC, MX, MTA-STS, TLS-RPT and BIMI since a previous run. Pass the `snapshots` object returned by the previous call as `previous`; the server stores nothing. The first call returns a baseline with no changes.

tools.name: watch_sending_domains
tools.description: Hosted monitoring. Register domains for a daily server-side check of SPF, DKIM, DMARC, MX, MTA-STS, TLS-RPT and BIMI; when something changes, the changes are POSTed as JSON to your https webhook_url. Free for up to 3 domains (renew every 30 days). For 4 to 20 domains in one watch, call without a pas

tools.name: flatten_spf
tools.description: Free. Replace the includes in a domain's SPF record with the IP ranges they resolve to, and return the TXT records to publish. Use it when an SPF record is at or over the 10-lookup limit.

tools.name: verify_email
tools.description: Check an email address: syntax, whether its domain accepts mail, typo suggestion, disposable and shared-mailbox flags. Checks the domain, not the individual inbox. Costs one credit with an API key (POST /v1/agent/provision returns a key with 100 free credits), or $0.01 USDC on Base per call over x40

tools.name: domain_intel
tools.description: Free. Registration data for one domain from the registry (RDAP): when it was registered and its age in days, expiry, registrar, status codes, nameservers and DNSSEC. Flags domains registered in the last 30 days, a strong spam and fraud signal, and domains about to expire.

tools.name: check_tls_certificate
tools.description: Free. The TLS certificate a host serves on port 443: whether it validates, issuer, names covered, expiry and days left.

tools.name: check_blocklists
tools.description: Free. Whether an IPv4 address, or a domain's MX and A addresses, are listed on the SpamCop and PSBL blocklists. Spamhaus and Barracuda are not queried (their terms require a subscription); the result says which lists were checked.

tools.name: analyze_email_authentication
tools.description: Free. Explain why an email passed or failed authentication or went to spam. Pass the raw message, or just its headers: checks DKIM signatures (verified when the body is included), whether the sending IP is authorized by SPF, DMARC alignment and policy, what the receiving server recorded, and delays

tools.name: get_x402_payment_endpoints
tools.description: List the paid HTTP endpoints, their prices in USDC on Base, and the free endpoints.

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "watch_sending_domains" references sensitive artifacts (api_key). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: verify_email · Private data: watch_sending_domains, flatten_spf, verify_email · Public sink: flatten_spf, verify_email, analyze_email_authentication · Destructive: monitor_sending_domains, watch_sending_domains.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: verify_email · Private data: watch_sending_domains, flatten_spf, verify_email · Public sink: flatten_spf, verify_email, analyze_email_authentication · Destructive: monitor_sending_domains, watch_sending_domains

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "inspect_domain_dns" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.

evidence.snippet: before: "Run a free real-time RFC 7208 SPF 10-DNS-lookup audit, DMARC policy (_dmarc) alignment check, and MX server inspection on any domain." → after: "Free. Audit one sending domain: MX hosts, SPF with every include expanded and the true DNS lookup count against the limit of 10, DMARC policy including inheritance from the parent domain, and published DKIM keys. Returns a grade and the fixes to make."

findings.remediation: Re-review the tool before continuing to trust it.
